text:
alex: Quick sync — need to prioritize incoming customer asks for private deployment packaging. Main asks: 1) zero-touch upgrades with DB migration rollback, 2) bring-your-own KMS + HSM + audit logs, 3) preserve customer IPs across migrations (VIP preservation), 4) airgapped installer that can apply signed security patches offline. Need launch criteria and tradeoffs documented by EOD.

sam: Quick clarifying Qs — which customers require IP preservation vs. just stable DNS? Is the ask per-tenant VIP or just SNAT/egress preservation? Also: zero-touch upgrades and airgapped installers push in opposite directions (automation vs manual firmware signing).

julia: Field intel: three customers called this week. Bank A (FinTech) = KMS + audit + signed bundles. Telco B = VIP persistence for NAT-heavy infra. Gov C = fully offline installer + FIPS HSM requirement. All flagged upgrade rollback guarantees as a blocker.

priya: I recommend priority ranking: security/compliance (KMS, audit) > upgrade downtime SLA (<30m) > IP persistence > offline installer UX. Put the revenue/contract size on the deck: https://short.link/priv-deploy-customer-grid

matt: Ops note: Customers expect a rollback option that completes in ~15m and ability to drain traffic. Our current operator can do rolling restarts but lacks DB schema rollback and coordinated drain hooks. That’s the biggest ops gap.

lina: Tech constraints: KMS/HSM plumbing is straightforward (TLS + keywrap + rotation UI). IP preservation is messy across clouds — often requires customer-controlled LB or a NAT solution on their edge; we can approximate with connection draining + stable target groups but not true VIP portability. Airgap installer = large QA + package signing + offline patch distribution.

alex: Proposed phased approach: 1) Wave 1 (GA): BYO-KMS + audit logs, documented network handshake, upgrade operator with canary + rollback (limited DB change patterns). 2) Wave 1.1: formalize IP-preservation patterns (customer LB templates + runbook). 3) Wave 2: airgapped signed bundles + offline patch tool. Need alignment on scope and resources.

sam: For upgrades I propose: canary rollout + automatic fallback. Canary gate = health checks + smoke inference test. Health check we use:
```
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq .status
```
If health != "ok" or sample latency > threshold or error rate > 5% in canary, trigger automatic revert.

julia: Draft launch criteria (for Wave 1): - automated canary rollout + verified rollback path tested end-to-end - smoke test suite (inference + storage) passing 99.9% in test clusters - documented network handshake checklist for customers + template IaC - support runbook and 24/7 oncall for first-week post-launch - legal & security sign-off for BYO-KMS flows

priya: Negotiation tactic: offer paid "upgrade assistance" for customers that need a 0-risk migration window. That lets us ship a leaner GA while addressing large customers' risk appetite.

deploy-bot: Reminder: please file RFC for "private-upgrade-operator" before EOD to unblock schedule. Template: /rfc new private-upgrade-operator. Also add coverage for DB-migration rollback scenarios.

alex: Action items: sam + lina own upgrade operator RFC; julia to draft tiered deployment bundles (core, core+KMS, core+upgrade-assist); priya to coordinate customer comms + negotiation scripts; matt to enumerate required runbook steps for rollback & drain; sync 2pm today in #product.

alex: TL;DR — ship secure KMS path + safe upgrade operator for GA, treat IP-preservation as a close-following requirement, and scope airgap for Wave 2. Please flag any downstream blockers in thread.
